title: Scheme-theoretic images of split tori are split tori
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group isomorphic over $F$ to $\mathbf G_m^r$, $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m$ is [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $T$ be a torus, let $H$ be any such group, and let $h:T\to H$ be a homomorphism. Suppose $h=j\circ u$, where $j:I\hookrightarrow H$ is a closed immersion of affine finite-type group schemes and $u:T\to I$ is faithfully flat. Here faithfully flat means that extension of scalars along $F[I]\to F[T]$ is exact and detects zero modules. Then $I$ is a torus. No smoothness or connectedness is assumed on $H$, and no smoothness or finiteness is assumed on $\ker h$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(b),(c), printed pp.233--234; Definition 12.14 and its following paragraph, printed p.236 (a quotient of a split torus is a split torus); Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.42, printed p.108, identifying the faithfully flat image factor with the quotient by the kernel.

proof.text: Choose $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. By [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria], identify its coordinate Hopf algebra with $B=F[\mathbf Z^r]$, whose basis is $e_m$ for $m\in\mathbf Z^r$, with $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, $\Delta(e_m)=e_m\otimes e_m$, $\epsilon(e_m)=1$ and $S(e_m)=e_{-m}$. These identifications concern the group law, not only the underlying scheme.

source.place: Examples 12.1--12.2 and Remark 12.6, pp.231--232; Definition 12.14, p.236.

proof.text: Put $C=F[I]$ and $i=u^*:C\to B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] with the zero ideal, $i$ is injective. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] to $I$ and $T$. Because $u$ is a group homomorphism, pulling back its multiplication, identity and inverse diagrams gives $\Delta_Bi=(i\otimes i)\Delta_C$, $\epsilon_Bi=\epsilon_C$ and $S_Bi=iS_C$. Thus $A=i(C)\subseteq B$ is a unital subalgebra stable under the antipode, and every $\Delta_B(a)$ is a finite sum $\sum_j b_j\otimes c_j$ with $b_j,c_j\in A$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 12.9, pp.233--234, coordinate-ring interpretation; injectivity: Stacks Tag 05CK (algebra.tex, lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective).

proof.text: For $m\in\mathbf Z^r$, let $\lambda_m:B\to F$ extract the $e_m$ coefficient. If $a=\sum_n a_ne_n\in A$ and $\Delta_B(a)=\sum_j b_j\otimes c_j$ as above, apply the linear map $x\otimes y\mapsto\lambda_m(y)x$, supplied by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. It gives $a_me_m=\sum_j\lambda_m(c_j)b_j\in A$. Therefore $a_m\ne0$ implies $e_m\in A$, by division by $a_m\in F^\times$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, proof (a) implies (b), p.235: coefficient extraction in the group-like basis; applied here to the coordinate subcoalgebra.

proof.text: Define $L=\{m\in\mathbf Z^r:e_m\in A\}$. The unit, multiplication and antipode formulas give $0\in L$, $m+n\in L$ for $m,n\in L$, and $-m\in L$ for $m\in L$; hence $L$ is a subgroup. Step 3 gives $A=\bigoplus_{m\in L}Fe_m$. The map $F[L]\to A$, $e_m\mapsto e_m$, is therefore a bijective algebra map, and the displayed formulas for $\Delta,\epsilon,S$ show directly on this basis that it preserves all Hopf operations.

source.place: Theorem 12.8, p.233, group-like basis construction; Remark 12.6, p.232.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], $C$, and hence $A$, is generated over $F$ by finitely many elements $a_1,\ldots,a_s$. Let $E$ be the union of their finite monomial supports. Step 3 shows $E\subseteq L$. Write $L_0$ for the subgroup generated by $E$. Each polynomial expression in the $a_i$ has support in $L_0$, because multiplication adds exponents and addition can only remove terms. If $m\in L$, then $e_m\in A$ is such a polynomial expression, so $m\in L_0$. Thus $L=L_0$ is finitely generated. This also covers $s=0$, when $A=F$ and $L=0$.

source.place: Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, (1) implies (2), with both affine opens the whole schemes; finite-support argument elaborates Milne Theorem 12.8, p.233.

proof.text: The subgroup $L\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$ is torsion-free: if $nm=0$ for $n>0$, then each integer coordinate of $m$ is zero. It is finitely generated by step 5, so [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] supplies a finite integral basis $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d$. Every $m\in L$ has a unique expansion $m=\sum_i n_i\ell_i$ with $n_i\in\mathbf Z$, including $d=0$.

source.place: Definition 12.14 and following paragraph, p.236: the lattice of a split torus is free of finite rank; finite-basis theorem as recorded in the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The basis gives mutually inverse Hopf algebra maps $F[\mathbf Z^d]\leftrightarrows F[L]$, sending $e_{(n_i)}$ to $e_{\sum_i n_i\ell_i}$ and using the unique coordinates for the inverse. Together with $C\simeq A\simeq F[L]$ these identify $C$ with $F[\mathbf Z^d]$ as a Hopf algebra. Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor] to both maps: their spectra are inverse group-scheme homomorphisms, since the functor preserves compositions and identities. By [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria], $I\simeq D_F(\mathbf Z^d)\simeq\mathbf G_m^d$. Thus $I$ is a torus. The proof used no property of $H$ or of $\ker h$ beyond the given factorization.

source.place: Theorem 12.8 and 12.9, pp.233--234; Definition 12.14 and following paragraph, p.236.

proof_origin.place: Theorems 12.8--12.9, pp.233--234, and Definition 12.14, p.236; direct coordinate-subcoalgebra elaboration using the coefficient calculation of Theorem 12.12, p.235, rather than quotient uniqueness.
